checks.name: Explicit binary coordinate and measurable full image
checks.finding: coordinate q b is the probability of q=true, valued in unitInterval. Measurability uses the actual probability-measure evaluation sigma-algebra and measurable q. liftBelief is the explicit (1-c) Dirac-zero + c Dirac-one probability measure and is measurably parameterized. Representatives satisfying q zero=false and q one=true prove coordinate(liftBelief c)=c, hence the real image is exactly [0,1], a closed set. This is an explicit binary construction, not an invocation of a general measurable-image or Borel-selector theorem.

checks.name: C1 common posterior version and correct almost-everywhere scope
checks.finding: The latent X is Standard Borel and nonempty, A is an arbitrary measurable space, and the deterministic observation has target Bool. Bool supplies both the CountableOrCountablyGenerated condition for C1 parameterized disintegration and the CountablyGenerated target condition for deterministic_comp_posterior. The proof combines the actual common C1 version with the existing posterior only observationLaw(b,a)-a.e. for each fixed (b,a). It then proves the pushforward posterior on Bool is Dirac y a.e. and uses Measure.map_congr to obtain the exact coordinate transition law. No common null set across all beliefs/actions is assumed, and no identity at zero-probability observations is invented.

checks.name: Closure is an original-source generating-test condition
checks.finding: ClosedTests requires equality of P(x,a)(q^-1{true}) for q-equivalent states. Since P is Markov and Bool is binary, the true singleton mass determines the entire pushed-forward row, including its complement. Equal belief coordinates determine equal Boolean pushforwards; integrating the closed source rows through a two-point representative then proves equal predictive observation laws. The closure assumption is neither an assumed belief quotient nor an assumed target transition kernel.

checks.name: Constructed measurable Markov quotient and uniqueness
checks.finding: quotientKernel is defined from the actual c1BeliefTransitionKernel by comapping the explicit measurable belief section and mapping coordinate. It is a measurable Kernel by construction and Markov because the underlying C1 kernel is Markov and coordinate measurable. Under ClosedTests, the factorization follows from the actual C1 coordinate law and predictive-law invariance. Uniqueness is forced at every c in [0,1] by testing liftBelief c, so it is exact equality of kernels rather than an unqualified a.e. uniqueness claim. The full-image hypothesis from the two explicit representatives is essential and retained.

checks.name: Converse and absence of circular premises
checks.finding: Given a factorization for every input probability belief and action, the proof tests Dirac x and Dirac x prime with equal q. Their coordinates agree, so the pushed-forward actual C1 laws agree. Evaluating the distinct coordinate vertex 1 recovers the true singleton observation mass, which equals the original source fibre probability. This proves ClosedTests without assuming that the candidate quotient is Markov. The forall-beliefs condition is stronger than a statement only on reachable beliefs and is explicitly present; no reachable-belief extrapolation is made.

checks.name: Actual finite-word tests and forward predictive sufficiency
checks.finding: testResponse is recursively defined from the original P rows and observation indicators for finite action-observation words; testExpectation integrates that response against the input belief. Source closure inductively makes each word response a function of q(x), and equal coordinates therefore imply equality for every such test. Markov normalization bounds the response and its expectation by one. The singleton-word bridge is explicitly proved equal to the original predictive observation probability. In the measurable closed setting used by the witness, the factored Boolean response is measurable. The generic module does not claim the converse predictive equivalence for every closed source.

checks.name: Witness canonical iff is supplied by a real separating probe
checks.finding: The witness uses State=Bool x Bool and the actual stochastic source built from a Bernoulli(1/4) noise. Its observed first-coordinate source rows are independent of the hidden second coordinate, proving ClosedTests. Action false preserves the observed bit, although hidden state remains stochastic. The concrete word [(false,true)] has expectation exactly coordinate. Equality of all finite-word tests therefore implies coordinate equality, while the generic forward theorem supplies the converse. Canonicality is precisely for this witness and chosen controlled observation tests; it is not a general minimal-memory theorem.

checks.name: Nontrivial stochastic hidden source
checks.finding: The numerical source is an actual Markov kernel obtained by pushing Bernoulli noise through advance. The proof computes hidden-bit flip mass exactly 1/4. The two Dirac aliases (false,false) and (false,true) have identical coordinates and all chosen future tests, yet different hidden states. Thus the example does not obtain predictive equivalence by assuming the latent process itself is a deterministic relabeling.

checks.name: Negative actual-source counterexample rules out the quotient
checks.finding: badSource is a separate explicit deterministic Markov kernel. Action true exposes the hidden bit as the next observed bit. Dirac beliefs at (false,false) and (false,true) share coordinate zero but yield next true-observation masses zero and one. Any all-beliefs factorization would imply ClosedTests and contradict these literal source rows. The theorem rules out every measurable Kernel factorization of the specified coordinate, even without requiring the target kernel to be Markov.

checks.name: Reward and safety readouts retain independent contracts
checks.finding: The positive reward bridge applies only to rewards explicitly of the form r(q x); because Bool is finite, integrability is established. The safety identity concerns the current belief probability of q=false, namely 1-c. The witness reward is observed-bit reward minus a known action cost and satisfies that contract. Hidden reward and hidden safety have no coordinate readout even among arbitrary functions: the equal-coordinate Dirac aliases give expectations/probabilities zero versus one. This directly demonstrates that predictive equivalence does not supply hidden objectives. No all-time safety, viability, value preservation, or optimal-control conclusion is smuggled into these readout identities.

assumptions_and_limits: General X may be Standard Borel, but the observation/generating-test alphabet in this result is specifically Bool and deterministic q; arbitrary noisy observations or arbitrary Borel predictive images are outside scope.
For the equivalence and uniqueness endpoint, two explicit points representing both observation classes are required. A constant or non-surjective q does not satisfy that endpoint contract.
Source P is a measurable Markov kernel. ClosedTests is an exact pointwise source-row equality for each action, not an estimated or almost-everywhere-on-initial-support condition.

C1 posterior identities are observation-a.e. for each fixed belief/action. The resulting integrated transition identity is exact for every belief/action; null posterior observations remain version-dependent.

The quotient descends the next-belief Markov kernel through the chosen coordinate for all probability beliefs. It is not asserted to be a lossless latent-state quotient, full posterior reconstruction, arbitrary-policy value equivalence, or globally minimal memory.
General source closure gives same-coordinate implies same finite-word tests. The reverse is proved only for the actual witness using its hold-observation probe, not for arbitrary closed P.

Finite-word identities concern the explicitly defined source tests. No new arbitrary-Borel canonical quotient, arbitrary infinite-history theorem, or independent full trajectory-law construction is asserted.

Safe-class probability is a present-belief readout, not a dynamic physical-safety theorem. Reward/safety factorization needs its own observation-measurable readout condition, and the hidden-readout counterexample proves that condition is substantive.

conclusion: CLEAR for the exact 498-line core and 197-line witness reviewed here. The common-version a.e. interface, original-source closure iff unique measurable Markov quotient, witness-only finite-word canonical iff, explicit no-quotient source, and independent reward/safety conditions are coherent and noncircular within the stated binary special case.
